newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Thai Danu and others too.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Thai Danu and others too.

text.p: Thai Danu Bank brought a hefty floating rate certficate of deposit issue into Asian debt markets on Tuesday, while other Asian borrowers opted for Euro and Yankee bonds.
Thai Danu Bank launched a two-tranche US$130 million FRCD issue due 2002.
The US$100 million tranche has put and call options in the third year. It pays a margin of 60 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an all-in return of 87 basis points.
The US$30 million tranche has annual put and call options. It pays a margin of 40 basis points over LIBOR and an all-in return of 58 basis points.
The issue was initially expected to be US$150 million in size. Pricing was a few basis points wider than anticipated.
The pricing is much wider than that of a similar deal launched for Thai Danu last March.
In that transaction, the one-year tranche paid an all-in of 42 basis points and the three-year tranche paid 60 basis points. That FRCD could not be called, however.

Weakness in the Thai banking sector has caused Thai bank issues to fall out of favour this year. Prices have widened in the secondary market, although traders have said that there is no sign of dumping.
Moody's announcement on February 14 that it might cut Thailand's A2 sovereign rating also has not helped the outlook for new issues, bankers said.
Most of the other action in Asian debt markets took place in Europe or the U.S.
Overnight, Korea Development Bank launched an innovative inflation-linked bond into the U.S. market via lead manager J.P. Morgan.
The US$300 million bond due 2002 pays a coupon of 3.4 percent over the U.S. consumer price index (CPI).
U.S. investors have shown more interest in such bonds since the U.S. Treasury decided to issue inflation-linked bonds earlier this year.
Later today, the US$500 million global bond for Philipines Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) will be priced.
The US$200 million 10-year bond is expected to price at 160-165 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, while the US$300 million 20-year tranche is seen pricing at 170-175 basis points over the benchmark.
Goldman Sachs and Citicorp are the leads.
Export-Import Bank of Korea set a 500 million mark FRN due 2002. The notes, which pay a margin of 15 basis points over LIBOR, were priced at 100.06 and re-offered at 99.96.
Fees are 10 basis points for selling, five basis points for management and underwriting and five basis points for listing.
DG Bank was the lead.
Merrill Lynch and Nomura jointly lead a US$750 million Euro-Asian bond for a unit of Abbey National Listing is in London and Hong Kong.
